clue.text: University affected you and me

parts.note: affected, theatrically exaggerated behaviour, is camp
you and me together are us

explanation.surface: A university's pretentious airs have rubbed off on the two of us.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the grounds of a college, standing for the university itself.

clue.text: In the end, this Titan didn't quite make it

indicators.note: falling just short means the phrase stops one letter before its finish

parts.note: in the end means finally, eventually

explanation.surface: A giant who, in the end, failed to reach his goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlas was the Greek Titan condemned to hold up the sky.

clue.text: Grant was a gift I had accepted

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so the gift word holds the contraction

parts.note: a gift is a present
I had contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: Someone says a grant was a gift they took.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulysses S. Grant was the eighteenth US head of state, an example of the office.

clue.text: Abroad the rents going up in this?

definitions.text: Abroad the rents going up in this?

parts.words: Abroad the rents going up in this?
parts.note: rents abroad keep rising in an ever-climbing, coiling inflationary pattern

explanation.surface: In other countries, rents keep soaring.
explanation.definitionFit: A wage-price or inflationary coil describes prices rising ever faster.

clue.text: This year involved great excitement

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of these two words are mixed together

explanation.surface: This past year has brought a great deal of excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Hysteria is a state of uncontrolled emotional frenzy, an extreme excitement.

clue.text: Opera ends all the anger that's aroused

indicators.note: aroused means stirred up, so the letters of these four words are churned

explanation.surface: An opera finishes off all the stirred-up anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Humperdinck's opera of the two children lost in the woods is a famous example of the form.

clue.text: Crooked money invested in worthless horse

parts.note: skew means slanting, crooked

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, so the money letter goes into the word for worthless

parts.note: worthless means bad
L is the pound sign, standing for money

explanation.surface: Dishonest money has been sunk into a useless racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: A skewbald is a horse with patches of white and a colour other than black.

clue.text: Mischievous little fellow drowned by rising river

indicators.note: drowned by means submerged inside, so the fellow goes into the river
in a down clue rising means the river's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Nile is the great river of Egypt
F is a short form of fellow

explanation.surface: A naughty little chap goes under in a river in flood.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means impish, playful in a sprite-like way.

clue.text: Make one at the wicket get up with some speed

parts.note: in cricket a batsman at the wicket is 'in'

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word get is read upwards

parts.note: rate means speed

explanation.surface: A cricketer at the crease is urged to speed things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To combine parts into a whole is to unify them into one.

clue.text: Loyalty for instance in marriage

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation goes inside the word for marriage

parts.note: a marriage is an alliance between two people or families
for instance is e.g., exempli gratia

explanation.surface: Faithfulness, for example, within a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegiance is faithful loyalty owed to a ruler, cause or partner.

clue.text: Two notes, that's a lot

parts.note: fa and te are two notes of the sol-fa scale
fa and te are two notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A remark that two musical notes add up to plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot is one's destiny, what fortune hands out.

clue.text: Like Henry Morgan, perhaps, 'e's lost it

parts.note: like means in the manner of, 'as'
Henry Morgan was a famous seventeenth-century Welsh buccaneer of the Caribbean

explanation.surface: A Cockney remark that some swashbuckler has lost his treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is itself an example: the speaker of "'e's" has dropped the breathed H of "he's", the very sound the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: The breathed H sound is what gets dropped when 'he's' becomes 'e's, so that sound has been lost.

clue.text: Gracious! An earlier model than C-nine did you say?

indicators.note: did you say asks us to hear the phrase spoken, not to read it

parts.note: B comes before C, so the earlier model would be a B-nine, spoken as 'bee nine'

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at an older model than the C-nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Gracious and benign both describe a kind, kindly disposed manner.

clue.text: Beware of place like Wookey Hole

explanation.surface: A warning to watch out at a Somerset tourist cavern.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin cave means 'beware' (as in cave canem); Wookey Hole, a show cavern in Somerset, England, is a hollow in rock.

clue.text: Record I put in a puzzle — "Say you're sorry"

indicators.note: put in means the record and I go inside the puzzle word

parts.note: to pose is to puzzle or baffle
a log is a record, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: Someone inserts a record into a puzzle and is told to apologise.
explanation.definitionFit: To express regret is what saying sorry does.

clue.text: The siren's welcome song

parts.note: not a mythical singer luring sailors but an air-raid siren's note, welcome because it means danger has passed

explanation.surface: A mythical singer's lovely tune welcoming sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: In wartime Britain a steady siren tone signalled that the raid was over and it was safe to emerge.

clue.text: Left out — I haven't a monster

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Excluded, someone complains they have no monster.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leviathan is the biblical sea beast, now any huge creature.

clue.text: Do many instruments produce the blues?

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a crossword stand-in for many
drums are percussion instruments

explanation.surface: A question whether lots of instruments bring on blues music.
explanation.definitionFit: The blues is a low, depressed mood, the same as being in the dumps.

clue.text: The infantry have to maintain some standing

parts.note: foot soldiers, the infantry, are collectively called foot
to maintain a position is to hold it

explanation.surface: Foot soldiers must keep a position on the battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: A secure position or toehold gives one some standing, a place to stand.

clue.text: Weapon — we switched the sight

parts.note: the V-1 flying bomb, written VI, was a German weapon of the Second World War

indicators.note: switched means the two letters of 'we' change places

explanation.surface: We swap the weapon in our gunsight.
explanation.definitionFit: A sight is something seen, a vista or prospect.

clue.text: Change does include copper coin

indicators.note: include means the copper symbol goes inside the reordered letters
change means alter, so the letters of does are reordered

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Small change does include copper coins.
explanation.definitionFit: The escudo was the former currency unit of Portugal.

clue.text: Dramatist takes care of a minor character

parts.note: care of is abbreviated c/o on envelopes
a ward is a minor under a guardian's protection

explanation.surface: A playwright looks after a small part in his play.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel Coward was an English playwright; 'minor character' looks theatrical but means a child in someone's care.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel Coward was a celebrated English playwright, so he is an example of a dramatist.

clue.text: House party up in Lincoln

indicators.note: in places the turned party inside the president's name

parts.note: Abraham Lincoln is known as Abe

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the party word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A house party is held upstairs in Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln looks like the English cathedral city, but it is Abraham Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: An abode is a dwelling, where one lives.

clue.text: Right? 'e's right in every investigation

parts.note: R again abbreviates right
taken letter by letter as written, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: in places the second right inside the word for every

parts.note: every one means each
R again abbreviates right

explanation.surface: A Cockney asks if he's right in every inquiry.
explanation.definitionFit: Research is systematic inquiry, a thorough study.

clue.text: Seek love, in short

indicators.note: in places the zero inside the word for short

parts.note: curt means short, abrupt
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A brief instruction to go looking for romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seek love' reads as the definition, but only 'Seek' is: love is the O.
explanation.definitionFit: To court trouble or favour is to seek it out or invite it.

clue.text: Miscible oils in store

indicators.note: miscible means able to be mixed, so the letters of oils are mixed up

explanation.surface: Oils that blend are kept in a storeroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A silo is a tower or pit for storing grain or fodder.

clue.text: Billy booked for being this?

parts.note: not a man arrested but Billy Liar, the novel by Keith Waterhouse: Billy put in a book, his title describing what he was

explanation.surface: Someone named Billy has been charged by the police for some offence.
explanation.definitionFit: A liar is by definition someone who is not telling the truth.

clue.text: Turning after river, several came to grief

indicators.note: came to grief means was wrecked, so the letters of several are broken up

explanation.surface: After turning off the river, several boats were wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: A turning round or turnabout is a change of direction.

clue.text: Make speech about national leader being decorated

indicators.note: about means around, so the speech word goes round the leading letter

parts.note: to orate is to make a speech

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of national

explanation.surface: A speech about a national leader being given an honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elaborately adorned is richly decorated.
